title: Single-org 403 on /api/admin/users deletion (and other global-scoped user actions)
answers: Why does a single-org Admin get 403 deleting a user via /api/admin/users even though they have users:delete?
Instance user management returns Forbidden in single-org deployments
DELETE /api/admin/users/:id works via Kubernetes User API but fails via legacy admin API
body:
Symptom: In single-org deployments, an org Admin with users:delete gets 403 on DELETE /api/admin/users/:id (and similarly create/enable/disable/quota/logout/auth-token endpoints), even though the same action succeeds through the Kubernetes User API.
Root cause: pkg/api/api.go registerRoutes forced authorization into org 0 via ac.UseGlobalOrg, ignoring the caller's current-organization permissions.
Fix pattern: swap the route authorizer from ac.UseGlobalOrg to ac.UseGlobalOrSingleOrg(hs.Cfg) — in single-org mode it evaluates permissions in the caller's current org, in multi-org mode it still requires global-context permissions.
Constraints: applies to /api/admin/users/* handlers registered in pkg/api/api.go (routing.Wrap(hs.Admin*)); do not apply to true org-management routes (those intentionally stay global-only) or to endpoints that already have an explicit non-permission guard (e.g. reqGrafanaAdmin), which must be kept alongside.
